title: 全然～ない — not at all ～
summary: Used with a negative verb or adjective to deny something completely: “not at all.” 全然 is an adverb placed before the predicate. It is used for verbs, adjectives and abilities.

patterns.gloss: 全然 + ない-form: 全然飲まない (don't drink at all)

patterns.form: 全然 ＋ 形容詞くない
patterns.gloss: 全然 + adjective negative: 全然おいしくない

body.p: 全然 raises the denial to zero: not even a little. 分からない means “I don't understand”, and 全然分からない means “I understand nothing at all”. It is stronger than あまり～ない (not very) and a bit casual.
In young people's speech you may hear 全然いい or 全然大丈夫 meaning “completely fine”, but for tests and formal writing, 全然 goes with a negative. Compare ちっとも～ない and まったく～ない.

examples.ja: お酒（さけ）は全然（ぜんぜん）飲（の）まない。
examples.tr: I don't drink alcohol at all.

examples.ja: この問題（もんだい）の意味（いみ）が全然（ぜんぜん）分（わ）からない。
examples.romaji: Kono mondai no imi ga zenzen wakaranai.
examples.tr: I don't understand the meaning of this problem at all.

examples.ja: 薬（くすり）を飲（の）んだのに、熱（ねつ）が全然（ぜんぜん）下（さ）がらない。
examples.romaji: Kusuri o nonda noni, netsu ga zenzen sagaranai.
examples.tr: Even though I took medicine, my fever won't go down at all.

pitfalls: In the standard grammar tested at JLPT, 全然 is used with a negative: 全然分からない. Do not use it with a plain positive.
Pair it with the predicate it negates; keep 全然 right before it.
